summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition of lanthanum aluminum oxide nano-laminates for electrical applications. The films were grown using a lanthanum precursor, trimethylaluminum, and water. The films showed low leakage current, good uniformity, and a high dielectric strength. The process involved alternating layers of lanthanum oxide and aluminum oxide to form a nanolaminate structure, which helped in reducing water diffusion and improving film quality.
evidence: Lanthanum aluminum oxide thin films were grown by atomic layer deposition from a lanthanum precursor, tris(N,N8-diisopropylacetamidinato!lanthanum (La(iPrAMD)3), trimethylaluminum and water. Smooth, amorphous films having compositions La0.5Al1.5O3 and La0.9Al1.1O3 were deposited on HF-last silicon... The growth temperatures were 300–330 °C. The nanolaminate structure consisted of m cycles of lanthanum oxide growth and n cycles of aluminum oxide growth. The films were characterized without postdeposition annealing.
